title: The Disappearance of Lars Mittank
summary: Josh and Chuck examine the 2014 disappearance of German engineer Lars Mittank (transcribed as Matonk in this episode) in Golden Sands, Bulgaria, near Varna. After a World Cup bar confrontation with rival soccer fans and an alleged beating that ruptured his eardrum, he was prescribed antibiotics, checked into a seedy hotel, phoned his mother, and then ran through Varna airport on CCTV, leaving his belongings behind and vanishing into a sunflower field near the A2 highway. The hosts walk through the leads and theories (untreated head injury, human trafficking, drug mule), the mother Sandra's searches and leads such as a trucker in Brandenburg and a homeless man in Dusseldorf, and the limits of available sources. The episode ends with a listener mail from a young listener named Hans.

segments.title: Opening and caveats on sources
segments.summary: Hosts introduce a true-crime disappearance case set in Bulgaria, note that information is hard to verify since Bulgarian case files are unavailable and much comes from Reddit and German sources, and mention that listener Dave Meischner suggested the story.

segments.title: Lars Mittank's background and Golden Sands
segments.summary: Lars Mittank, a German engineer and only child from northern Germany who loved Werder Bremen, vanished on July 8, 2014, in Golden Sands, a Black Sea resort near Varna, Bulgaria. He had been caring for his father after a stroke and was persuaded by his mother to take a week-long trip with friends.

segments.title: The trip, World Cup bar confrontation, and the ear injury
segments.summary: During the trip Lars ate lightly and was the life of the party with friends Tim Schultz and Paul Roman. At a bar watching a World Cup match, verbal confrontation with FC Byron fans occurred. Later Lars returned claiming he was jumped and his ear was punched; a doctor diagnosed a ruptured eardrum and prescribed antibiotics, and a specialist advised surgery in Germany.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before the story continues.

segments.title: Friends leave and Lars checks into Hotel Color
segments.summary: Friends flew home while Lars stayed behind because of his ear and flight concerns. He checked into the seedy Hotel Color in Varna after other hotels were full, where the front desk photocopied his credit card. He called his mother several times, including a call from a hillside where he said four men were after him, and texted her about an antibiotic.

segments.title: Western Union request and airport medical visit
segments.summary: Lars asked his mother for five hundred euros via Western Union, which was left untouched. He then visited an airport medical center, where the doctor gave conflicting accounts of what happened, including a possible airport worker or construction worker entering the exam room, before Lars left running.

segments.title: Airport CCTV and the run into the sunflower field
segments.summary: CCTV footage shows Lars running out of the airport with no bags, reportedly leaving his wallet, phone and passport behind, passing police officers, and jumping a barbed wire fence into a sunflower field near the A2 highway. Hosts discuss the footage and whether he appeared to be fleeing for his life.

segments.title: Investigation, leads, and the mother's search
segments.summary: Police and Interpol involvement was frustrating and the case received limited coverage at first. Sandra Mittank hired a Bulgarian lawyer, tracked about fifteen German expatriates, and followed online leads such as a man in Brazil (Anton Pilpa, a different missing man), a trucker in Brandenburg, and a homeless man in Dusseldorf who was ruled out within two hours.

segments.title: Theories: head injury, trafficking, drug mule
segments.summary: Hosts discuss theories including an untreated head injury or concussion causing memory loss and erratic behavior, a possible human trafficking connection, and a drug mule theory, which they find unlikely since no drugs were found. They note Lars was described as happy and loving Germany, which makes voluntary disappearance unlikely.

segments.title: Wrap-up
segments.summary: Hosts close the case discussion and credit Dave Meischner for suggesting the episode.

segments.title: Listener mail from Hans
segments.summary: A parent shares a drawing and letter from their second-grade son Hans, who listens to the show at bedtime and asked about a football episode.
